#4194. Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy Review: Beautiful, But Not Quite Blooming

Pikmin 4’s Switch 2 Edition looks stunning in 4K and Dandori Academy is fun, but slower loads and recycled content make this upgrade feel barebones.

As a German, I have a lot of appreciation for efficiency, and Pikmin 4 now comes with an entire game mode dedicated to it. Dandori – the Japanese term for forward planning and effective organisation – was always going to be right up my alley on that basis alone. Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition includes the Dandori Academy, and it is the main selling point for the DLC. It arrives three years after the original Pikmin 4 first arrived on the Switch.

Miyamoto announces Pikmin Day as Pikmin 4 prepares to be released on the Nintendo Switch 2 in November.

Pikmin 4 has been a huge success for Nintendo, and it's the bestselling entry in the franchise to date. I'll be the first to admit, though, that it's also a bit of a divisive one: many long-time players weren't too keen on the cuter look, or the fact that it no longer quite feels like you're stranded on an alien planet. Oatchi, the cute, derpy looking rescue pup, also changes the ways of how you interact with the world and the Pikmin quite drastically, making some of the classic Pikmin mechanics much less of a priority. With that in mind, a hardware touch-up seemed like the perfect opportunity to give the game some extra love. But can the Switch 2 Edition make the most of it?

Full disclosure: I was very kindly given a review code, and I spent about two hours with the new features, playing docked on my Switch 2. I will say that I wasn't able to take one of the Dandori Academy exams myself, as I played outside of the weekend – but more on that a little later.

First things first: the graphics look absolutely amazing. When docked, Pikmin 4 now runs in a stunning native 4K resolution, which makes it one of the few real 4K games on Switch 2 so far. Every leaf, puddle and tiny Pikmin face looks so crisp and lovely, and I truly found myself just stopping to admire the scenery more than once.

Sadly, that's where the technical improvements end. There's no improvement to the framerate whatsoever (it's still 30fps), though it seems that a lot of the game's logic is tied to that 30fps, so I can at least understand why. What I can't quite understand is that the load times are actually slower than in the original Switch game, and that's noticeable throughout. I am hopeful that a patch will sort this out, because truth be told, it does take the shine off an otherwise very pretty upgrade.

Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is one of, if not the, best third-party ports for Nintendo Switch 2.

The thing that surprised me most, though, is the lack of mouse controls. It often feels like Nintendo tries to shoehorn mouse mode in wherever they possibly can, and yet Pikmin 4 – one of the few games where it would actually make so much sense for aiming and throwing – doesn't have it at all. That is an odd decision, and I really hope it's something that gets added later down the line.

First things first: the graphics look absolutely amazing. When docked, Pikmin 4 now runs in a stunning native 4K resolution, which makes it one of the few real 4K games on Switch 2 so far.

What I do like is the new Howl-Out feature, which lets you give commands to Oatchi using the Switch 2's microphone. It works decently well, and it's a really cute addition. I will say, though, that I live in a pretty calm place with no background noise, so I'm not entirely sure how well it would hold up in a household with kids or pets running around. And if you want to take on your friends in a Dandori Battle, you can now do so via GameShare, which is a lovely touch for anyone who doesn't have a second copy lying around.

As previously mentioned, the main addition here is Dandori Academy, and I love the idea: clear a stage's treasure as quickly as possible, on different maps and with different Pikmin available to you. It's so incredibly fun! The time trials are split into three difficulty options, so even the more casual story-enjoyers will find something for them here, whilst the Master Medal looks to be decently hard to get, which means the hardcore Dandori experts will have plenty to sink their teeth into, too.

Dandori Academy is where all that forward planning truly comes into its own. Whilst you don't really need all that much of it in the main game, here every second counts, and every Pikmin needs to be exactly where it's supposed to be. Before I knew it, I was trying really hard to beat my previous high score (and then the one after that, and the one after that).

From Pikmin 4 to Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne, these are ten strategy games where the user score is higher than the critical score.

Some of the challenges are based on Pikmin Bloom, so whilst a few of the first six maps have been reused, I'm happy to report that not everything is recycled. Overall, the challenges are fine: nothing mind-blowing, but quite fun, and still very cute. Taking the “exams” unlocks medals and in-game rewards.

What is annoying, however, is that you can only take those exams on the weekend, which really is not ideal – and is exactly why I didn't get to take one myself. On top of that, the 72 challenges are arriving gradually over the next year, which breaks down to around six per month. If you manage to sort them all on the first weekend, that leaves you with three weekends of nothing to do, which feels lacking if the goal is to keep players engaged.

Beyond Dandori Academy, there isn't all that much new to discover. There are no additions to the main story whatsoever, and much of the new content leans quite heavily on what was already available in the base game. Personally, I would've preferred more story content, and three years on from the original release, the whole package does feel barebones.

Truth be told, it's one of the weakest Switch 2 Editions so far. That being said, $10 is a pretty small price to pay for a gorgeous 4K glow-up, a few small features, and a mode that will keep you entertained for some time. If a patch sorts out those loading times, I'd say it's most definitely worth picking up.

Ultimately, Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy takes a game that was more than ready for a hardware touch-up and doesn't quite do as much with it as it could have. The foundations are lovely, and my Pikmin have never looked better – I just wish they'd been given a little more room to grow.

Wuhu Island is back, and so is the magic. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort finally recaptures the charm that made me fall for this series years ago.

#4193. Battlefield Labs is coming back for a short session to test out next week's Battlefield 6 update, and you can expect more tests in the future, too

Battlefield Labs is evolving, as it reopens its doors for its next - unusual - session.

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios announced a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

#4192. Death Stranding Isolations Animated Series Gets New Teaser Trailer

A new teaser trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an upcoming animated series coming exclusively to Disney+ and Hulu next year, premiered during Kojima Productions’ 10th Anniversary Exhibition Beyond the Strand. The series was first announced last year.

Death Stranding Isolations tells an original story in the Death Stranding universe set immediately after the events of the first game. Isolations is created by Japanese animation studio E&H Production (Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet, Magic Knight Rayerath) and directed by Takayuki Sano.  Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer.

Today’s teaser video provides the following story synopsis:

The Death Stranding—a catastrophic series of explosions caused when the dead crept into our world and collided with the living.

In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation—among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate.

In Death Stranding, legendary game creator Hideo Kojima brought you a haunting vision of a shattered world. Now, that world expands into new frontiers with a brand-new animation series.

Under the guidance of director Takayuki Sano, world-class hand-drawn animations have been brought to life by renowned studio “E&H production” (NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET, the Magic Knight Rayearth television series).

The story is set in North America immediately after Sam—the protagonist of the game—reconnects the continent by means of the Chiral Network. However, as America is reborn from the ashes, the renewed connections that bind it together bring about new and unforeseen consequences.

In this tumultuous new landscape, there are some who walk a different path to the one chosen by Sam and his Bridges comrades: a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning; a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction; a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life...and of course, the girl who chose to sever all ties with the outside world...Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize.

Death Stranding Isolations is coming to Disney+ and Hulu in 2027. It’s one of the three planned big-screen adaptations of the series. An animated movie called Death Stranding: Mosquito (working title) is also in the works alongside a live-action Death Stranding film by A24.

For more on Death Stranding, check out our reviews for the first game and its 2025 sequel. You can also read the latest update on Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth-espionage game, Physint.

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

#4190. Dota 2 returns to Esports World Cup 2027 as PARIVISION chase a first repeat title

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be announced later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

#4189. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4188. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

#4187. XBOX Team Up With DJ Khaled For GTA 6 Promotion

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

GTA 6 is just days away, and the highly anticipated release is leaving players looking for an excuse to take time off work to explore Leonida, Rockstar’s take on the state of Florida. XBOX is stepping in to give gamers a day off work, but it’s unlikely their strategy will work with your boss.

As we gear up to launch, a multitude of celebration events have already been revealed, including exclusive Twitch rewards for tuning into GTA 6 streams for the remainder of November, and even an in-person concert in Miami.

The funeral for your dearly-departed, totally real best friend Ann Alibi is being held at a Queensland KFC, totally coincidentally on GTA6 launch day.

DJ Khaled has extended his resume and rebranded to Dr XBOX, and is handing out sick notes for those who want to play GTA 6 on launch day and avoid any other responsibilities.

“After extensive research (and a whole lot of gaming), I’ve come to one conclusion: there’s a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency around the world.” According to Dr XBOX, the cure is as simple as taking the day off work.

The promotion doesn’t explicitly mention GTA 6, but there are several clues. First of all, DJ Khaled is sporting an XBOX-branded lab coat and showing off his XBOX University certificate by a poolside, wearing a casual leaf-patterned outfit, and is signing doctor’s notes “from the sunny shores of tropical Miami.”

Without naming GTA 6, the Dr XBOX says, “a big week in gaming is coming, and I don’t want anybody missing a single moment. We’ve got games to play, worlds to explore, achievements to unlock and victories to celebrate.” GTA 6 is undoubtedly the biggest release not only this month, but in recent years, so it’s easy to piece together what XBOX is getting at here.

Since PlayStation has promotional rights over GTA 6, it’s not surprising to see XBOX trying to take advantage of this huge release through as many unofficial paths as possible.

To get your sick note from Dr XBOX, you must visit the dedicated Dr XBOX website and enter your name. You could always use your gamertag for that gaming feel if you wish, but you’re unable to enter numbers or symbols.

According to Dr XBOX, the cure is as simple as taking the day off work.

Once you’ve typed in your name and hit enter, the note will say you’re experiencing a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency, along with the need to avoid work, your symptoms, and the doctor’s recommendations. The note is signed by Dr XBOX and has an official XBOX stamp of approval. You can then share your note with friends, on social media, and even attach it to an email to your boss, but it’s unlikely to fool anyone.

A recent survey pointed towards 12.5 million American gamers planning to adjust their schedules for the big day. Of course, the doctor’s note has no official standing, but it’s a fun little gimmick to get into the GTA 6 spirit. XBOX’s disclaimer even outlines that “XBOX is not responsible if your employer doesn’t have a sense of humor.”

The wait is almost over, as GTA 6 will launch worldwide on November 19, 2026, on XBOX Series X|S and PlayStation 5.

Pocketpair saved everyone the trouble of calling in sick by giving its employees five days to enjoy GTA6.

#4185. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4184. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4183. GTA 6 Gives Players 62 Reasons to Take Up Birdwatching

Most of us already have a plan for our first few hours in GTA 6. Steal a car, see how the police react, explore Vice City, and maybe get around to the story eventually. But Rockstar is also giving us a good reason to leave the car parked and pull out a pair of binoculars instead.

GTA 6 will have 62 different bird species to discover, and you can record them in a wildlife logbook. The detail emerged during The Guardian's visit to Rockstar North, when journalist Keza MacDonald noticed a gull sitting on a post near the beach. Jason pulled out his binoculars, and the bird was added to the logbook.

It's a small interaction, but it suggests there will be plenty to occupy us in Leonida besides robberies and police chases.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

We already knew Rockstar was putting a lot of effort into Leonida's wildlife. Earlier reports pointed to more than 170 animal species across the state, including over 60 birds, roughly 30 land mammals, and a variety of reptiles and aquatic creatures. The exact count of 62 birds isn't a massive surprise, then. What's more interesting is that we now know you can actively look for them and keep a record of what you've spotted.

It's one thing to see birds flying overhead, but a logbook gives you a reason to stop and identify them instead of driving straight past.

Leonida has plenty of places where this could be fun. We've seen coastal areas, the wetlands of the Grassrivers, and the tropical scenery of the Leonida Keys. Looking for wildlife could be a good excuse to explore places that might otherwise get overlooked in favor of Vice City's streets. Rockstar hasn't said whether certain species are tied to particular habitats, though. A logbook might be all it takes to get players to stop and appreciate the wildlife.

A logbook might be all it takes to get players to stop and appreciate the wildlife.

We don't know whether finding all 62 species earns a reward, whether some birds are particularly rare, or whether spotting them depends on the time of day. The game's dynamic weather system raises another question, but there's no confirmation that weather affects wildlife sightings.

Actual birdwatchers are already looking forward to GTA 6 for this exact reason. In a November 15 thread on Reddit's r/birding community, one user asked whether anyone else was excited to catalog the game's birds. They added that their planned crime spree would have to wait.

Some commenters hope there's an achievement for spotting every species. Others brought up Red Dead Redemption 2, which got a few of them interested in birdwatching in real life.

If you've spent much time in Rockstar's western, you can probably relate. You could lose an afternoon studying animals, watching how they behaved, and filling out the compendium instead of doing whatever Arthur Morgan was supposed to be doing. A trip through the woods often turned into something completely different from what you'd originally planned.

In fact, this is one of several reasons why I never got around to finishing Red Dead Redemption 2 despite multiple attempts. I made it a priority to complete every hunting-related achievement and log every single wild animal present in the game.

And considering how much time I spent documenting wildlife in Red Dead Redemption 2, I can only imagine how much more distracting GTA 6 will be. After all, we're moving from the relatively sparse world of 1899 to a densely populated, modern-day Leonida, with far more going on around us. Between all the wildlife, activities, and countless other details Rockstar has packed into the game, I wouldn't be surprised if I ended up neglecting the story all over again.

Vice City's roads, crowds, and nightlife will probably take up most of our time at first. But I can easily imagine heading out to explore, spotting a bird I haven't logged yet, and forgetting what I was supposed to be doing in the first place.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The robberies can wait when there's a gull on the beach that needs identifying.

#4182. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

The 2026 calendar offers a reference point for the circuit’s rhythm. MSI ran from 28 June to 12 July, and Worlds from 15 October to 14 November. Riot has not confirmed whether the 2027 events will follow similar windows.

#4181. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4180. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4179. Fortress Saga tier list - Ranking every hero

Updated on November 17th, 2026 - Version: 2.1.20

Want to know who you should deploy to protect your walking fortress? In our Fortress Saga tier list, we ranked all the available heroes so you can have a clear idea of who should be out on the field and who you shouldn't bother with (at all).

There are a lot of heroes in Fortress Saga. Many of them are good, but you do not have access to all of the best picks from the beginning. So, as is the case most of the time, you will probably end up upgrading some of the lower-rarity ones because you have no other choice.

Even if that is the case, the heroes that are ranked at the top of this Fortress Saga tier list are the ones you should try obtaining and upgrading ASAP. The second you get some of them, the rest is history. That's when the real game begins.

Since the game has been around for a while in Japan, this tier list is based on that, and I have adapted it to the Global server. I have also added explanations for some of the heroes underneath each tier, so if you're curious as to why some of the heroes rank the way they do, all you have to do is keep reading.  Did you know we have the latest Fortress Saga codes? Go ahead and redeem them for some free goodies! Can you reroll in Fortress Saga? Some people might wonder about rerolling in this game, and that is just not worth your time. At the beginning, you don't have access to all the heroes anyway, so rerolling would just delete all your progress, account and everything else, while not getting any "good" heroes anyway. So, don't bother thinking about rerolling in Fortress Saga.

Now that we've got that out of the way, let's dive into the actual tier list so you can have a clear idea of which heroes to use on your team! S+ Tier  |  S tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Heroes at the top of the Fortress Saga tier list are a must-upgrade. I recommend you start with the first one you get (which is probably the only non-Legendary) and then upgrade the others as you get them.

Violet can summon Shadow Soldiers who fight battles for you. She is extremely good, especially since her passive can grant her summons a lot more damage and they can benefit from additional stats granted by other heroes. Malleus is a hero who works great against large clusters of enemies. He will jump to the area with the most enemies and deal a lot of damage, pulling them together. He can also buff allies with the Machina trait. Styria is a support, and she will recover allies' HP like no other. She can also shield allies, and just by being deployed, she will passively increase all allies' HP.

Winter is a beast in terms of AoE damage. This also knocks enemies back, and if the same enemy is hit by the skill four times, they become frozen. Zelos can deal some really good damage, but can also apply really good crowd control on enemies (Fear). He can stun bosses, so this hero works pretty well against them. He can passively absorb some HP based on the damage dealt, so he has a lot of sustain. Jibril is a burst damage dealer, and once her passive is unlocked, the flurry of projectiles can fly even further. She is great regardless of whether you face a single target or multiple enemies.

Soba amplifies allies' ATK with his passive, can deal quite high damage to enemies, and knocks them down. It's a decent hero if you don't have any better ones. Scarecrow is a Unique (blue) hero who is pretty good at all things. It can heal allies and then transform all the excess healing into a shield. Since it's a Unique hero, it can be upgraded fairly quickly, so that's why it lands in this tier. Ravia is a great AoE damage dealer and inflicts bleed on the opponent's hit. When they have low enough HP, she can execute them. It's great, especially against large waves of enemies, and when paired with more AoE heroes.

Bruce deals AoE damage based on his ATK. His passive amplifies all heroes' ATK, so that's great for a Unique hero. Loxia can apply crowd control on enemies hit. She is decent if you don't have any better damage dealers/passive buffers, preferably some from the higher-rated tiers. Bernhard comes with good AoE damage that shreds the enemies' DEF. He can also taunt them, and once you activate his passive, he will also become immune to crowd control. He could land in a higher tier if he has the right team (and versus the right enemies).

As you can see, a lot of the other heroes land at the bottom of the Fortress Saga tier list. These are the heroes you should not bother with at all, regardless of their rank/upgrade status. There are plenty of Unique and Rare heroes in the higher tiers that you should focus on upgrading, so in my opinion, don't bother with these at all.

If you need to use some of them until you get an upgrade, that's fine, but otherwise, just try not to invest anything more than necessary into them because it's a waste of resources.

You can take a peek at our Disney Pixel RPG tier list and other similar ranking guides, like this Castle Duels tier list. We have a lot of them, surely there's something that will draw your attention.

#4175. Garden Tower Defense tier list - Master your plants

Are you eager to learn which plants give you the most bang for your buck? Whether that's the Dragon Fruit or the Lemon Tree, our Garden Tower Defense tier list ranks all the plants you can summon!

Updated on November 17th, 2026 - Version: 1.73

With its simple gameplay at first glance, Garden Tower Defense doesn't exactly scream "challenging"; however, the moment you dive into your very first stage, you'll be convinced otherwise (not to mention totally get schooled and humbled).

With such difficult opponents, you'll soon wonder which units you should deploy to keep your defence intact - and that's where our Garden Tower Defense tier list comes into play. We've ranked all the plants you can summon right now, so you don't have to think twice between deploying your Dragon Fruit or Lemon Tree. Yes, we have a clear winner among these two (spoiler: it's the Lemon Tree).

So, are you eager to learn which plants give you the most bang for your buck? You'll find out on the following pages - or better yet, why not claim the latest Garden Tower Defense codes too, so you can really get a proper head start?

Right then - let's take a look at the complete Garden TD tier list! S+ Tier  |  S Tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

As you might have guessed, some of the strongest plants in our Garden Tower Defense tier list belong right here. Here you'll find powerful AoE damage dealers like all the Big Mushroom varieties, which are simply fun to play!

We also have the Lucky Clover, which is a Support, and probably one of the best ones out there. As the name suggests, it boosts your Luck.

Hellroot is one absolutely amazing AoE, which also deals DoT (burn). It's definitely the best of both worlds for AoE and ST.

Corn is okay, but it is not as good as Juggercorn, which not only has higher flat stats, but also better range.

Doompetal is one of my personal favourites, and even though it is not in the S+ tier, it can still deal considerable damage, especially against single targets.

The Laser Plant is lower-rarity than most of the others, but it works almost as well. It costs as much as the Confusion Plant to deploy (1500), but it deals good damage and has a pretty low cooldown.

Some of the plants in the A tier are pretty good, but despite some of them being rarer than others, they aren't quite as "wow". The Glass Sunflower is okay, but its damage is not that great.

As for the Pesticider, it could rank higher, but it has such a high deploy cost (3000) that it's simply not practical - there are better and cheaper options out there for sure.

The Venus Floortrap is a rare plant, and you shouldn't confuse it with the Venus Flytrap, which is a lot rarer. The Floortrap is a "Trap", and it does pretty high damage considering how common it is.

Many of these plants are viable early on, especially the Ghost Pepper - this one does really good damage for its rarity, and it's also super cheap (400).

Cherries might not seem that strong early on, but if you max them, they can deal significant damage to any opponent, especially bosses.

Durian is known for its signature "aroma" (a.k.a. insane smell), hence earning its place in our Garden Tower Defense tier list. It deals AoE damage, but it's ranked in the B tier because it has a pretty high cost for what it does.

The plants in this tier you won't use for very long. The Tomato is your starter plant, and although it's super cheap, it doesn't do much - it focuses on a single target, so you will swap them out as soon as you get something better.

As for the rest, it's pretty much the same story for all of them.

And there you have it - we've always known how beneficial plants are in real life, but our Garden Tower Defense tier list takes it a step further by ranking which ones are even more beneficial than others, doesn't it?

As you can probably tell, we do love ranking stuff over here, so if you're curious, why not take a peek at our Anime Rangers X tier list and our Anime Saga tier list for more?

#4173. Bilibili Gaming beat all four LCK teams to win Worlds 2026 and end Korean title run

Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

Bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in New York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

The final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

For Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

The runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy said the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting plan.

Gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

Worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

Our first Summoner’s Cup. It’s finally coming home.

— Bilibili Gaming (@BilibiliGaming) November 15, 2026

The calendar also tilts towards China. First Stand will open the 2027 season as First Stand: All In, a one-off expanded event. Riot calls it the largest tournament it has ever produced. The event was first announced for Southeast Asia. That region will now host First Stand in 2028 instead.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.

#4171. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

Aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

Miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

Finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.
