#4169. Devolver Digital is Running a Giveaway for Anyone Willing to Delete their GTA 6 Preload

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Devolver Digital has always had something of a reputation amongst game publishers as a wild card, a cheeky band who will take unusual, often silly measures to promote their upcoming games. Said measures can range from creating entire standalone games like Devolverland Expo to hitching a ride on whatever the current trend is in pop culture, and whether or not they work, you have to respect the publisher’s sheer commitment to the bit.

Now, if I asked you, “what’s the biggest buzz in pop culture right now,” the answer would undoubtedly be Grand Theft Auto 6. The game is finally launching in two days after over a decade of development, and everyone who plans on playing has likely had their preloads locked and loaded since they opened up last week. However, here’s the big question: would you be willing to part with all 212 GB of that preload for a chance to win a copy of a pixel art sidescroller?

On the official Devolver Digital X, formerly Twitter account, the publisher announced its latest marketing stunt: an official giveaway contest for its next upcoming title, Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed, which just so happens to be launching the same day as GTA 6 on November 19. Do you want to win? All you have to do is bin your preload.

With 62 bird species to discover and a wildlife logbook to fill, GTA 6 might turn even the most dedicated criminals into birdwatchers.

As Devolver Digital explains in its X post, it’s offering the chance to win a free copy of Volvy Adventure: Reslimed to anyone who reposts with the hashtag “#MakeRoomForVolvy,” alongside a clip of them deleting their GTA 6 preload from their console. Said clip can either be direct captured footage from the console in question, or just a filmed clip taken with your phone, but either way, that preload has to go bye-bye if you want a chance to win.

A follow-up post notes that Volvy’s Adventure is exclusively launching for PC, so while the filmed clip does need to be of a preload deletion on a console, you will need a PC to actually redeem and play the game through Steam if you win.

That preload has to go bye-bye if you want a chance to win.

Obviously, the contest doesn’t require you to skip playing GTA 6 altogether; you can immediately preload the game again after deleting it, and Devolver won’t care. You just have to show your commitment to the bit, and considering the game’s massive preload has reportedly taken some users several days to download, that’s a bigger commitment for some than others.

Even so, the contest has drawn some interest, with a number of retweeters deleting their preloads in the name of Volvy, though others have apparently already pre-ordered Volvy’s Adventure on Steam and weren’t planning on getting GTA 6 anyway. Life is funny like that sometimes.

The release of Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t just a product launch, it’s a full-on social phenomenon. Everyone is talking about it, even those completely outside of the gaming culture sphere, and businesses around the world are bracing for large swaths of their employees to spontaneously develop the flu on release day to skip work.

Not dissimilar to Devolver, many other businesses in and out of the gaming industry are looking for their own ways to capitalize on this major pop culture moment. Just today, KFC’s Australian branch announced it would be holding a fake funeral to give people an excuse to call out of work, alongside offering free delivery throughout the country on launch day.

Similarly, DJ Khaled is running a promotion alongside XBOX where he’s signing sick day notes under the guise of “Dr. XBOX,” warning that many people are experiencing a severe “vitamin G deficiency.”

I’m honestly uncertain whether this mass marketing push will slow once GTA 6 actually comes out, or just ramps up further, at least for a month or so afterward.

#4168. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4163. Late Submissions Dominate Game of the Year Nominees

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

The Game Awards 2026 is almost here, and the nominees for the coveted Game of the Year prize have been revealed, with most of the entries launching near the end of the year, and one of them isn’t even out yet.

While not as prestigious as the Academy Awards, The Game Awards is the industry’s best way to reward beloved titles, as well as shine a light on games that might not have been played as much, all with a heavy dose of commercials and reveals for upcoming releases.

XBOX is collaborating with DJ Khaled to sign sick notes to get players a day off work to play GTA 6, although the game isn't explicitly mentioned.

The official The Game Awards Twitter/X account has announced the six titles up for nomination for Game of the Year. Curiously, most of the titles that made the shortlist only came out recently, with one that is not available to the general public for another two days.

Here are your six nominees for Game of the Year. #TheGameAwards streaming live on Thursday, December 10.

The six nominees for Game of the Year are 007 First Light by IO Interactive, Control Resonant by Remedy/Annapurna, Grand Theft Auto 6 by Rockstar Games, Phantom Blade Zero by G-Game, Resident Evil Requiem by Capcom, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by Nintendo. Most of those titles came out very recently, and many players haven't even had a chance to finish them.

Of the six nominees, only two came out in the first half of the year. 007 First Light came out on May 27, and Resident Evil Requiem launched on February 27. Meanwhile, Control Resonant launched in late September, Phantom Blade Zero was released in October, while the others came out in November.

The six nominees for Game of the Year are 007 First Light by IO Interactive, Control Resonant by Remedy/Annapurna, Grand Theft Auto 6 by Rockstar Games, Phantom Blade Zero by G-Game, Resident Evil Requiem by Capcom, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by Nintendo.

Many fans are surprised that Grand Theft Auto VI is included in the nominations, but that, The Game Awards takes nominations from gaming outlets (including DualShockers), so being available to the general public is not part of the equation.

It’s not unheard of for the Game of the Year award to be dominated by late releases. After all, companies prefer to release titles near the end of the year so they can be purchased for the holiday season. There will certainly be a lot of people who won’t be returning to Vice City or Hyrule until December 25.

Clearly, Geoff Keighley and the people who nominated Grand Theft Auto 6 are confident that it has what it takes to win the Game of the Year award, and, to be fair, it’s a pretty safe bet, based on Rockstar’s history and reputation. The numerous delays for Grand Theft Auto 6 proved that Rockstar and Take-Two wanted to make sure the game was just right before releasing it, and fans are confident it will pay off.

Even if Control Resonant takes a surprise win, Rockstar and Take-Two are the victors, due to the sheer amount of money Grand Theft Auto 6 has brought in so far. The award is nice, but the millions of dollars are a little nicer.

We're not just talking about Grand Theft Auto VI and Ocarina of Time, but up to seven video games that could sweep The Game Awards.

#4161. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4159. EDward Gaming part with CHICHOO and nobody as Champions core breaks up before 2027

EDward Gaming have lost captain nobody and CHICHOO, two days after releasing Smoggy to Bilibili Gaming. The VCT China partner team must now rebuild before the China Kickoff in Hangzhou in January.

EDward Gaming have parted ways with CHICHOO and captain nobody, two pillars of the side that won VALORANT Champions 2024. Both players left the VCT China partner team on the same day. EDG announced both exits on Weibo. Their exits end a five-year spell at the organisation.

The departures follow quickly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming. Within a week, three players had gone from the EDG roster. No replacements have been named.

Wang ‘nobody’ Senxu joined EDG on 7 September 2021. He served as the team’s captain and in-game leader. He had started out as the side’s Initiator before taking on those leadership duties. CHICHOO, whose full name is Wan Shunzhi, played the Controller role. Alongside CHICHOO, he formed the core of the only Chinese team to win Champions. That title, sealed on 25 August 2024, made EDG the first organisation from China, and from Asia, to lift the trophy. The team’s total winnings stand at roughly $1,592,287.

The pair were still central to the side in 2026. At Masters London, CHICHOO and nobody each played 12 maps. Their average combat scores were 179 and 184 respectively. EDG finished third in London and earned $125,000. Their run ended with a 0-3 defeat to Leviatán in the lower bracket final on 20 June 2026.

Where nobody goes next is not yet confirmed. Sheep Esports reported, citing sources, that he is expected to join Trace Esports for 2027. Trace’s Kai and deLb are said to be under contract until the end of 2027. If that move happens, nobody and Smoggy would both start the new season with different organisations.

The timing is awkward for EDG. The organisation was named a VCT partner team on 21 October, on a two-year contract. That deal now begins with a heavily changed roster.

The China Kickoff is an S-Tier LAN event. It is organised by TJ Sports, Hero Esports and Riot Games. The league’s partner sides make up eight places in the field, with the remaining four split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants. EDG will need a settled line-up in place to compete there.

#4158. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4157. Infinity Kingdom Tier List - Best Immortals and a few tips

Updated on November 17th, 2026 - Version  3.0.6 - Latest Addition: Jadwiga (Grace of Heaven)

Have you been wondering who the best immortals are in Infinity Kingdom? Then you're in the right place. Below, we're going to share our complete Infinity Kingdom tier list of immortals and give you everything you need to know about each one of them, so you can pick the best for your team.

There are quite a lot of immortals in the game, and let's be honest - if you're a F2P player, you'll have a pretty tough time picking just a handful of them to invest in. While premium players have it way easier, we'll go through some of the best immortals and explain which you should upgrade first, and which will not be worth the time in the long run.

Before we dive into the Infinity Kingdom tier list, though, let me give you a few tips about the immortals, so you'll know exactly why I've ranked them the way I did. You can invest in anything (pretty much), but it will be a lot easier to just stick to a few good ones Investing in any hero will never be a waste once you gain access to the lab because you can choose to reborn them when they have fulfilled their purpose. However, it will be easier if you just stick to the right heroes from the get-go. Try to think ahead about what teams you want to use and which heroes will fit best. You also need to take into consideration the way you will play. Are you going to invest a lot of money in the heroes and teams? Are you going to be a F2P player and rely only on what you get for free?

These aspects can have a pretty big impact on the heroes that you will use, so make sure that you consider everything. Of course, if you're planning to just casually play the game, you can go for any hero and then just reborn them in the lab when the time comes. Stick to one troop when you're at the beginning At the very start, you want to stick to one troop. Boost that troop in every way that you can, and use it for all content. It's going to help you complete a lot of it without much effort. Always summon 10x times, never do individual summons Whenever you collect nine Philosopher's Stones, you will be able to summon 10 times. Normally, one summon will cost you one Stone, but if you choose to save nine Stones, you can pull 10 times from the gacha. This is the best option you have, so hold onto your Philosopher's Stones whenever you can, because it will guarantee you one Elite or Epic unit within the 10 units that you pull. Join an Alliance and don't use your speedups until you've received help from your Alliance mates This feature is super important for upgrading your kingdom quickly, for a number of reasons. Firstly, the very first time you join an alliance, you'll receive some Gems for free, so that's definitely useful, no matter if you're a F2P player or not. Secondly, you will be able to ask your Alliance mates for help, and that will drastically reduce the construction or upgrade time for anything. Finally, you'll save up a lot of speedups if you just give it a few minutes (for the Alliance mates to have a chance to offer their help) before going for the 1-button speedup.

Of course, you can also take a shortcut and use some of these Infinity Kingdom codes for a quick boost!

Now that you're all caught up, let's check out our Infinity Kingdom tier list of the best immortals!

The Immortals in this category are some of the best in the game. They can usually be used with all the units/troops, and they will buff all of your soldiers no matter what. It's never a waste investing in them, so by all means start upgrading these immortals as soon as you get them.

These Immortals will be viable from the first moment you get them, so even if it takes a little bit of time to upgrade them, you won't have to worry - they'll still be good even if they only have one skill unlocked.

The following Immortals are as good as the S-tier options, but they're mainly dedicated to a specific type of troop. They might not be as great if you don't assign them to their required troops, so that's why they fall under the S-tier. However, if you give them the units that they're good for, they are easily S+ tier.

Feel free to upgrade all of these units as long as they fit your play style and team formations. Otherwise, you can just wait before spending all your resources in leveling and upgrading them.

The immortals that fall under this tier are mainly great F2P choices, since they can be easily obtained without having to spend any money. They can be highly effective in a number of team/immortal comps, so you can invest in them regardless.

If you're not sure how you will go about the game, just know that it's never a waste to upgrade these immortals. You will definitely end up using them at some point.

Most of these units you will rarely see once you reach the late game. They are useful early on, but start to fall off fairly quickly. You shouldn't invest in them unless you don't have any other choice. There are better units that you can pick on this tier list.

The heroes in this tier are not ideal for the late game. You want to swap them out for an alternative as soon as possible, since their kit is very weak compared to the other heroes.

There is always a bottom tier in any game. This Infinity Kingdom tier list is no exception to that rule. The immortals that fall under the D tier are some of the weakest out there. They will not do you any good, and it's not worth investing anything at all into them. You're better off just waiting for another summon and even getting a C-tier hero, rather than use one of the D-tier immortals.

#4156. The Elder Scrolls VI Has An Official Subtitle And It's 'Sentinel'

The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.

The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.

The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

#4155. Pokémon GO's Duolingo Crossover Gives Language Learners a Shot at Shiny Lucario

Duolingo's green owl already has a reputation for making sure you don't forget your lessons. Now, it's offering Pokémon GO players a different incentive to open the app – a chance at Shiny Lucario.

Redeem a code for free Pikachu Crocs in Pokémon GO. Gengar and Jigglypuff avatar items are available with purchases of the corresponding Crocs.

Pokémon GO and Duolingo have teamed up for Duo's Pokémon Party, a limited-time event that rewards language practice with Pokémon-themed avatar outfits and special Timed Research. You won't get Lucario just for finishing a lesson, but completing lessons on seven different days will earn you a chance to encounter one.

The crossover began on November 17, according to the official Pokémon GO announcement, and you can take part regardless of which Duolingo course you're studying.

First, update Duolingo and join Duo's Pokémon Party in the app. Completing a lesson in any course earns your first reward, with more rewards available for studying on additional days. These include up to four Pokémon-themed suits for your Duolingo avatar. The suits are cosmetic rewards within Duolingo, not outfits for your Pokémon GO trainer. To get something in Pokémon GO itself, you'll need the research code.

The outfits include Poké Ball, Pokémon GO, Chatot, and Pikachu suits, so there's something to collect even if you aren't interested in the Timed Research. There's a catch with those rewards, though – they won't stay in your Duolingo wardrobe forever. Duolingo says the suits will expire on March 31, 2027, meaning you'll lose access to them even if you've already unlocked all four.

For the Pokémon GO reward, you'll need to complete at least one lesson on seven different days. They don't have to be consecutive, but seven lessons in one sitting won't count. Once you've met the requirement, you'll receive a code for the collaboration's Timed Research.

Redeem that code on the Pokémon GO Web Store's redemption page using the account linked to your game. The Timed Research will then become available in Pokémon GO.

You don't have to begin a new language course, either. If you've been working through one already, those lessons count toward the seven-day requirement. The important part is showing up on seven separate days.

The research carries the language-learning idea into Pokémon GO. You'll choose a language for the tasks, which will appear in that language rather than the one you normally use in-game. Professor Willow will offer hints if you get stuck.

Completing the tasks rewards you with XP, Stardust, and encounters with Pikachu, Meowth, Chatot, and Lucario. Each Pokémon comes with a special background and can appear in its Shiny form. A Shiny Lucario isn't guaranteed, of course, but it's a pretty tempting reward for keeping up with your lessons.

A Shiny Lucario isn't guaranteed, of course, but it's a pretty tempting reward for keeping up with your lessons.

There's also a language tag for certain Pokémon caught through the research. Tapping it on their summary page shows their names in different languages. It's a small detail, but at least the partnership brings some language learning into Pokémon GO rather than stopping at a promotional code.

There are three deadlines to remember. You must join Duo's Pokémon Party by December 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time. After joining, you have until December 29 at 11:59 p.m. local time to complete lessons on seven different days and claim your Duolingo rewards.

You'll also need to finish the Pokémon GO Timed Research and claim its rewards by December 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time. Redeeming the code alone isn't enough, so don't leave the research until the last minute.

I haven't kept up with my Duolingo lessons lately, but this might finally get me to resume them. Apparently, the chance of a Shiny Lucario is more motivating than another reminder from Duo.

And even if the Shiny hunt doesn't work out, seven days of lessons isn't a huge commitment. Whether I'll manage to keep the habit going after the event is another matter.

It's quite refreshing to be able to make some actual progress in a mobile title without opening my wallet. Thanks, Pokemon GO.

Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup. The move pairs him again with former NRG teammate brawk as Sentinels try to return to international events after missing them all in 2026.

The Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and said keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

The signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

That spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko said on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a new team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap quickly.

keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

#4152. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

From a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was important that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

In both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

Wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

After the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

After the game launched, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

As a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

For resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel important for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that quickly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

The last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

Wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#4149. Holiday Gift Guide 2026

With the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50

If you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The new Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some users with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25

Many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but currently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059

Many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

#4148. 10 Ocarina of Time Remake Moments That Made Me Feel Like a Kid Again

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Growing up with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time means carrying a very special set of memories with you. I first played this adventure as a kid, when the idea of growing up, taking responsibility, and dealing with the more bittersweet aspects of life (just like Link) felt very different from what it does today.

Back then, I was simply a child exploring Hyrule, discovering secrets, and wondering what would happen next. Now, coming back to this world as an adult, I find myself looking at everything through a completely different lens (of Truth, I suppose!).

But despite seeing this adventure with more mature eyes, there were moments when I completely forgot about everything around me, and, for a few seconds, I wasn't a grown-up playing a remake on a modern console anymore. I was that same kid sitting on the floor of my bedroom, playing Ocarina of Time on a CRT television and getting lost in a world that felt magical. So, let's get a little nostalgic today and revisit the 10 remake moments that made me feel like a kid again.

I dare you not to shed a few tears when you hear the first notes of The Legend of Zelda's iconic main theme – it is that very moment when you finally realize this remake is real, and you're about to embark on a journey that has meant so much to you for so many years.

There's something incredibly powerful about hearing a familiar melody return with a fresh presentation. Suddenly, all those childhood memories come rushing back, and you remember exactly why you fell in love with this series in the first place.

Thankfully, the remake also brings enough improvements and new touches to make the experience feel fresh. It's a wonderful balance between revisiting something familiar and getting excited about discovering it all over again. And we're only at the title screen!

Some games have opening sequences that are simply too good to get old, no matter how many times you replay them. And I feel exactly that way about the introductory hours of Ocarina of Time. Running around Kokiri Forest, learning about this world through the eyes of its young inhabitants, and slowly figuring out what we're supposed to do is still a delight.

There's so much to love about this section: getting those cryptic instructions from Navi, finding the Kokiri Sword and Hylian Shield, and finally making our way into the Great Deku Tree. It does such a wonderful job of introducing the world and making us feel like we're part of this little community before the adventure truly begins.

Honestly, just thinking about it makes me want to grab a bag of snacks, sit on my favorite childhood beanbag, and spend another afternoon exploring the forest. Some things never change, do they?

I think we can all agree that this is a canon event for every Ocarina of Time player: leaving Kokiri Forest and immediately sprinting toward Hyrule Castle, desperately trying to reach it before nightfall. Otherwise, you'll find yourself surrounded by those creepy Stalchildren, and nobody wants that on their first trip through Hyrule Field!

Thankfully, that particular rush isn't quite the same in the remake, giving us a much calmer first experience with the enormous landscape. And while I love that frantic moment from the original, I have to admit that I really needed those few extra seconds to stop and appreciate the view.

Seeing Hyrule Field with this new presentation, taking in the scenery, and realizing just how far the world stretches ahead of us was surprisingly emotional. For once, I wasn't in a hurry to reach the castle. I just wanted to stand there for a little while and enjoy being back.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

Using the ocarina as a gameplay mechanic has always been one of my favorite things about the original Ocarina of Time. There's something special about learning a melody, remembering its notes, and realizing that you can use music to interact with the world around you.

Still, I had my doubts about whether the remake could recreate that same feeling – and, well, it did! Besides, there’s a new feature that lets us sing or even play an actual musical instrument to trigger a song makes the experience feel even more personal.

It's such a magical way to interact with one of the most iconic elements of the adventure, turning something we usually do with buttons into an actual musical experience, making every familiar melody feel a little more special.

That first moment when Link pulls the Master Sword from its pedestal is unforgettable. After spending so much time as a child, we're suddenly transported seven years into the future, and everything we thought we knew about Hyrule has changed.

But the real shock comes when we walk out of the Temple of Time and see what has happened to Castle Town. The once-bustling streets are now in ruins, the atmosphere is completely different, and the familiar kingdom has become a much darker place.

And seeing all of this with the remake's new visuals gave me chills all over again. For a moment, I felt the rush of running to Kakariko Village to check if everyone was still there – since it literally hit me like the first time.

One of the most enjoyable moments of playing as Adult Link in the original game is finally reclaiming Lon Lon Ranch from the terrible Ingo. After all that trouble, getting reunited with Epona, now fully grown, feels like such a rewarding moment. Playing Epona's Song, challenging Ingo to a race, and finally winning back the ranch is an experience I could never get tired of.

And the remake makes this moment just as magical as I remember it! I won't even tell you how many tears I shed during this sequence, especially when Epona makes that iconic jump over the fence, right above Ingo's head, to escape the ranch. That little moment brought the biggest smile to my face.

Having a horse in a video game was such a cool concept back then, and somehow, it still feels just as cool today. There's something incredibly freeing about riding across Hyrule with Epona by your side, and I don't think I'll ever get tired of it.

Nintendo has expanded one of the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most heartbreaking side stories.

The symbolism and challenge behind fighting Dark Link in the middle of the Water Temple already make this encounter memorable. You're facing a mysterious version of yourself in what is the most challenging dungeon in the entire game. But the remake somehow managed to make this already iconic fight even more impressive.

And if you've faced him yourself, you probably know exactly what I'm talking about! Dark Link can actually dodge one of your attacks by jumping onto your Master Sword and balancing himself on the blade. It only lasts a few seconds, but it's such an incredible detail that I couldn't help but stare in disbelief the first time it happened.

It's one of those moments when you're simultaneously nervous and amazed by what you're seeing. You can almost feel the tension through the controller as you try to figure out how to deal with this little menace.

I love pointing out how The Legend of Zelda titles occasionally pretend to be horror experiences, and Ocarina of Time has some particularly memorable examples. The Bottom of the Well is easily one of them, throwing Link into a disturbing underground area filled with fake walls and some of the most unsettling enemies in the game.

And let's not forget the ReDeads and Dead Hand! Seriously, who thought putting those things in a game for children was a good idea? I still remember how uncomfortable I felt exploring this place as a kid, never quite knowing what might be waiting around the next corner.

Returning to the Well with improved visuals didn't make things any less terrifying, either. If anything, seeing all those creepy details in greater clarity made the experience even worse. I was just as scared as I was all those years ago!

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

Boss fights are one of the most memorable parts of any Zelda adventure, and Kotake and Koume are easily among my personal favorites. The twin witches offer a genuinely fun battle, but what makes them so special is how much personality they bring to the encounter. They're not just dangerous enemies, but also absolutely hilarious!

Their constant bickering, especially when they start arguing over which one of them is younger, never fails to make me laugh. It's such a silly little interaction, but it gives the two characters so much charm and makes the entire encounter even more memorable.

And the remake takes things a step further with dedicated cutscenes and voice acting, making the sisters even more entertaining. Their performances are spot on, and I found myself grinning like an idiot every time they started arguing.

Reaching the climax of Ocarina of Time is already an emotional experience, but climbing Ganon's Tower is one of those moments that stays with you forever. And I'll never forget ascending that final staircase before confronting Ganondorf, with the intense organ music gradually growing louder as we approach the villain.

But here's the brilliant detail: Ganondorf is actually the one playing that music! It's such a simple touch, but one that made players lose their minds back in the day, especially talking about a time when games weren't always experimenting with environmental storytelling in this way.

The remake recreates the moment beautifully, preserving all the tension and impact while giving us an even more impressive look at the scene. And then there's Ganondorf himself, and seeing his updated design in all its glory only makes the encounter more intimidating! It's easily one of my favorite interpretations of the King of Evil.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the most beloved games of all time, but these remakes might be just as meaningful to fans.

#4147. Mo.Co weapons tier list

Updated on November 17th, 2026 - Version: 13.5.1

When you dive into this action-packed RPG, you might be curious to know exactly how you can get good and how you can make your character stronger. The first step in that direction is following this mo.co tier list, where I ranked all the weapons in the game.

Weapons are a HUGE deal, for the main reason that you can get exclusive skills (or rather, attacks) that make you either deal more single-target damage, more AoE damage, or even grant some other type of neat skills.

This mo.co tier list will give you a detailed description of each weapon you can equip, and also rank them based on how strong they are. Oh, and don't worry if you only have the starter weapons, because those rank pretty well!  How to get the best setup? By the best setup, I mean picking a weapon and the Gadgets that have a good synergy together. For instance, if you want to pick the Speedshot weapon (which is single-target), you want a Gadget that will allow you to deal some AoE damage (like the Multi Zapper or Smart Fireworks, for instance). It all comes down to how you build your character for both bosses (single target) and regular mobs (AoE).

What is the best weapon in mo.co? While there is no "best" weapon, there are some that are significantly better, especially when we're talking about the later stages where the bosses are tougher. Of course, if you team up with a few players, you can make things a lot easier. However, if you want to shine on your own, this mo.co tier list should give you a clearer idea about the weapons that are considered top-tier. S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Speedshot is a ranged ST weapon that scales a lot better with Attack Speed. You will activate the SPEED mode after 10 attacks, which will greatly boost your attack speed, as long as you're continuously attacking enemies. In prolonged fights, it is top-tier.

Jaded Blades is kind of an assassin-type weapon. You will deal incredibly high single-target DPS, and with the Dash Attack, you'll have even more bossing prowess. It is mostly used for bosses.

Spinsickle is a personal favourite - it lets you deal AoE damage, and similar to Speedshot in a way, once you enter SPIN mode, you'll be able to attack enemies constantly. What makes it stand out is that while you're in SPEED mode, you will be able to dodge some of the attacks directed your way.

Techno Fists is not an outstanding weapon in mo.co, but it is okay-ish for both ST and AoE. It's great because of the stun you will get from the combo attack, which can apply to regular enemies.

The Wolf Stick is a great weapon for DPS. This one can summon a pet, it looks amazing, and when you play solo, it is one of the best, since the wolf will tank in your stead.

Buzz-Kill is another weapon that lets you summon something to aid you in battle. After every 4 attacks, you can summon 1 bee (up to 3 bees in total), which will attack enemies. It can be great for dealing with mobs since Buzz-Kill also has a short-ranged AoE attack.

Monster Slugger is a good AoE weapon, although it sits in the B tier. The main reason it doesn't rank higher is that while you will have a lot of AoE damage, your ST damage will have to be supplemented from something like the Monster Taser.

Toothpick & Shield is the tank weapon in mo.co. From this, you'll take decreased damage from enemies, and you will also have a short-range AoE attack. After getting hit 15 times, you'll deal area damage and stun enemies in range.

Portable Portal goes hand in hand with your rightmost Gadget. For this one, you want a Gadget with a relatively short cooldown, because its cooldown is based on that. Also, once you activate the skill, you will be able to use that Gadget for free.

Staff of Good Vibes is a healer's weapon, as you probably guessed from the name. It is not super commonly used, unless you want to play as a healer, and want to do it from the start, regardless of what other gear you have. It's currently standing at the bottom of the mo.co weapons tier list because there are better alternatives.

CPU Bomb is like a weaker Techno Fists. It will deal long-range AoE damage, and after every 8 attacks, it will throw a mega bomb that deals damage and stuns non-boss enemies.

Medicine Ball is another healer weapon that automatically heals an ally every 3 attacks. It deals close-range AoE damage, so it is quite a situational weapon.

Of course, that's not all - we have a ton of similar lists for you, like this Persona 5: The Phantom X tier list; and if you're more into older releases, take a peek at this Last Cloudia tier list too!

#4146. Heartopia finally gets a release date... on everything but Steam

Heartopia may very well be the first big game you play in 2026.

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

Interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

If you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

#4145. Devolver Digital Runs Free Game Contest Asking People To Delete GTA 6

Forget games being praised for releasing in the same month as GTA 6 - there’s an indie game bold enough to launch on the same day. Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed launches on November 19, and if you delete your GTA 6 preload, Devolver Digital might give you the game for free.

For years, Devolver has joked that it would release a game on the same day as GTA 6. Even when GTA 6 got delayed (twice), Devolver altered course along with it. Turns out it wasn’t a joke either, as here we are with two days to go, and Volvy’s Adventure, published by Devolver, will launch on the same day as what might end up being the biggest video game ever.

GTA 6 has consumed so much of the oxygen in the video game room that, predictably, getting people excited about Volvy has been nigh on impossible. It’s entirely likely this is the first time you’ve even heard of it. That’s why Devolver is turning up the heat and bringing out the big guns by giving Volvy’s Adventure away for free - but only if you delete your GTA 6 preload.

While everyone else is avoiding GTA 6, Devolver Digital is coming out swinging

“Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA 6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam,” the post on Devolver’s Twitter reads. It’s even paired with a clip of someone, presumably from the publisher's team, showing you how it’s done, which honestly, after how long it took my terrible internet to download all 212 GB of it, sent a shiver down my spine.

To be clear, if you like the look of Volvy’s Adventure and you’re seriously considering deleting GTA 6 for it, doing so doesn’t guarantee you’ll get a copy for free. Removing GTA 6 from your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S merely enters you into a giveaway to be in with a chance of getting Devolver’s new game for free, and there has been no indication of just how many copies the publisher plans on handing out.

Volvy’s Adventure is also the polar opposite of GTA 6 when it comes to launch platforms. While Rockstar’s big game will only be available on consoles, Volvy’s Adventure is exclusively available on Steam. If you don’t have a PC or a Steam Machine, then deleting your GTA 6 preload and sharing the evidence with Devolver will, at best, get you a Steam code that’s useless to you. Hey, maybe you can give it to a friend.

If you don’t have GTA 6 loaded up already, Devolver did offer one person the chance to enter by sharing evidence of them biting into a raw onion. I’m unsure if that offer is open to everyone.

It’s also worth noting to those in awe right now that might not fully understand what’s happening here that Devolver isn’t asking you to delete GTA 6 and throw away $80 for the chance to win a game that costs a fraction of that price (it’s $3.74 right now). Once the preload has been deleted, you can just re-download the game. The thing is, a game that big takes a long time to download, and at this late stage, depending on your internet speed, the longer you leave it, the more risk there is of GTA 6 not being ready to play when it unlocks in your region.

The theory that codes in boxes are being used to avoid leaks at all costs just became a little bit more credible.
