#4063. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

#4062. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

For more on Marathon, check out our review.

#4061. Watch the Battlefield 6 Season 2 gameplay reveal here

As promised, our first look at the next Battlefield 6 and Redsec season is nearly upon us.

After a one-month delay, we’re finally days away now from the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 of live service. The second season is being revealed today, following weeks of teasers, and some Battlefield Labs testing of the first new map arriving with the new season.

It’s all going to kick off with a gameplay reveal, which is set to stream live later today.

As we’ve come to expect, the Season 2 reveal will take place via a YouTube premiere. It’s set to kick off live at 8am PT, 11am ET, 4pm GMT on the official Battlefield channel on YouTube - and embedded below. Today’s reveal will also be followed by a more detailed roadmap of Season 2, which will give us a much better idea about the volume and cadence of content we can expect.

Season 2 goes live February 17, kicking off a new chapter in the continued conflict between NATO and Pax Armata. The medium-large new map, Contaminated, will be available immediately at the season’s launch. Contaminated takes placed in the mountains of Germany, centered around a once NATO-owned airbase.

VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this new season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

Look forward to more coverage from us as more details are revealed later today.

#4060. GTA 6 Subscription Will Include NBA 2K27 for Free on PS5

One month of GTA+ bundled into GTA 6 pre-orders

If you've pre-ordered GTA 6, did you take note of what bonuses you got with that? A one-month membership to GTA+, a subscription service from Rockstar, is bundled with all GTA 6 pre-orders, and that offer gets even better next week.

From 27th November 2026 until 15th January 2027, basketball simulator NBA 2K27 will be added to GTA+, providing a fully playable version of the standard edition. This is just like PS Plus Extra, except it's specific to games developed by Rockstar and participating publishers, like 2K.

Here are all the other games already included in a GTA+ membership:

Guide GTA Online: All GTA+ Games and Benefits

Everything you need to know about GTA's subscription

Guide GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

When you pre-order GTA 6, you automatically receive a code to redeem one month of GTA+. If you have not already claimed it, then you can save it for when NBA 2K27 is included and give it a go along with all the other titles included.

It'll be included in the subscription service until 15th January 2027. GTA+ costs £6.99 / $7.99 per month.

Just be aware that activating the code triggers a standard subscription once the initial period is over, so you need to turn off automatic renewals.

Once the online portion of GTA 6 is available, the GTA+ membership will become more valuable, as demonstrated by the current GTA Online. You get plenty of benefits in-game when you have a subscription.

#4059. Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores.

That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day."

There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes. Be sure to read about how GTA VI will target 30 FPS gameplay on all consoles, too.

#4058. Talking Point: As Xbox Celebrates Its 25th Anniversary, What Are Your Hopes For The Next 25 Years?

Maybe we'll be looking back on this in 2051!

The celebrations for Xbox's official 25th anniversary roll on! We've finally arrived at November 15th, which marks the exact date when the original Xbox launched all the way back in 2001. How time flies!

Of course, this is a great chance to reflect on everything that's happened over the past 25 years, which we've been doing in various articles throughout the month (and indeed the year), but it's also an opportunity to think about the next 25 years and where Xbox as a brand might be headed in the future.

I think the cynical view, and perhaps the logical view, is that Xbox won't exist by the time we get to 2051. Let's not forget that PlayStation was still in its infancy 25 years ago, SEGA had just got out of the console business after being a major player for so long, and Nintendo hadn't even released the GameCube in North America until November 18th of 2001.

Feature 25 Years Later, How Many Of These Original Xbox Launch Titles Have You Played?

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

In other words, 25 years is a very long time, and we've seen many ups and downs from Xbox throughout its history. The glory days of Halo, Xbox Live and the Xbox 360 were followed up by a horribly botched Xbox One launch, and the Xbox Series era has been summed up as everything from extremely promising to extremely disappointing, now hovering somewhere in the 'cautiously optimistic' territory for some Xbox fans since Asha Sharma took the helm earlier in 2026.

While console sales might be down, and the Xbox CEO keeps talking about a need to "return to growth", there's every reason to believe Xbox might still be a powerhouse in 25 years' time. Microsoft's backing is obviously a big aspect of that — assuming the brand never gets sold off — but so is the mountain of incredible first-party IP (Minecraft, Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, etc.) that should continue to rake in money over the next decade at least, coupled with the ability to innovate in the hardware space and eventually win back some market share with handhelds and consoles.

Realistically, the answer to all of this is that we don't have an answer - it's impossible to predict a future that's still 25 years out, especially when Xbox's mission statement appears to have changed on an almost yearly basis during the 2020s. There's no doubt that Xbox will face many challenges in the 25 years that are ahead and it'll be forced to adapt and innovate along the way, but I wouldn't be surprised if we're still talking about it in 2051!

For what it's worth, here's what Xbox boss Asha Sharma said on this topic a few days ago:

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this. [..] A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

#4057. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4056. Shigeru Miyamoto To Receive The Inaugural 'Legend Award' At The 30th D.I.C.E. Awards

Award will be presented only once per decade

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has announced that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, said the following:

“Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards."

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the company would even exist today without his creations.

He most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a new demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

#4055. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4054. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4052. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

#4051. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4050. 'The Ultimate Gaming Machine' - Xbox Reveals Tons Of New Project Helix Information

Also clarifying that it's definitely a console and not a PC

As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations today, we've been treated to a new digital version of a magazine that was given out at Seattle FanFest earlier this week, available to read in full over on the official Xbox Wire website.

The bit that's getting most attention concerns Xbox Project Helix - the new next-gen console that's currently in the works over at Xbox HQ. The brand's VP of Next Generation, Jason Ronald, shares tons of new information across four pages in the magazine, helping to give us a better idea of what to expect from the upcoming console.

There's one section in particular that's getting all the interest on social media right now, where he clarifies that Project Helix is definitely a console that can play PC games, and definitely not a PC that happens to play console games.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Beyond this, Ronald talks in depth about loads of other aspects of what they're aiming for with Project Helix, and as mentioned, there's so much detail that it spreads across four pages of the magazine.

In the interest of highlighting as much as possible though, we thought we'd transcribe all of most notable quotes from the magazine down below, whereas you can read the added context inside of the magazine article itself.

Here are more of the key bits from the magazine article:

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine - one that removes all barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

"We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics - it's really about gameplay innovation. It's about deeper immersion. It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

"When I think about what makes a console magical, it's that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don't have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings - things like that. The hardware and the experience is entirely designed around playing games."

"The very first next-generation conversations we had were with all of our first-party studios. That was absolutely foundational to the design of what we've done with Project Helix - talking about where they saw the future of game design going, where they saw the future of their franchises going, and what was constraining their creative ambition."

"With Xbox One, I think we got so focused on expanding our aperture that we lost sight of what truly is magical, which is players, developers, and the games that they love. We have to build the best platform for game developers to deliver their creative vision."

"The other thing, and I think this is something that is unique about Xbox, is we have to be connected to the community. A lot of the features that people have come to love and expect from Xbox have actually been driven directly by community feedback. I think that's really core to the soul of who Xbox is, because if you're in touch with your player base, you never go wrong if you focus on what their needs are."

"It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable."

"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

"The ROG Xbox Ally was really an opportunity for us to learn alongside our player base with a lot of these concepts and the ideas that we had: being able to play libraries from across multiple different storefronts, understanding how PC games and console games can show up together in a unified library. The feedback that we've gotten from players has fundamentally informed and altered our plans of how it actually shows up in a future console. Players shared where we met the mark and areas we needed to improve or approach differently. So absolutely, we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix - but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix."

Sorry for the wall of quotes, but we thought you might find all of this pretty interesting! It's not even the full extent of what Ronald had to say, as he also touched on the importance of game preservation to the Xbox platform in general, as well as how Project Helix will seemingly have a bespoke UI, but one that still feels familiar to Xbox fans.

Of course, we're still waiting on concrete details about what Helix will look like, how much it'll cost, how significant the PC integration will be, and loads of other things that will give us a much better picture of how it'll shape up.

It seems like we won't be getting that this year though, and if rumours are to be believed, Xbox might even be releasing a first-party handheld in 2027 before the Project Helix console in 2028. Who knows... plans can always change.

For now, let us know what you think about this latest info on Xbox Project Helix down below, and we definitely recommend reading the full Xbox 25th anniversary magazine for yourself - we wish we could buy one to be honest!

Honestly, whilst any new information is welcome, there is not a lot to be learned here. I have 3 questions:

I'd like to know whether it has a disc-drive because I have an extensive Blu-ray film collection (2000+ films), and I currently use my Series X to play them. I'm not fussed about the capability to play physical games because I have been all digital since the beginning of the Xbox One era. If it does not come with a disc-drive, then one that can be added (much like with the PS5) would be good. It's not a deal breaker for me because I can always just buy a 4K Blu-ray player, but it would be better to have just Helix and a PS6 under my television, rather than a Blu-ray player as well.

I have a gaming PC that I do not use for gaming right now, so all I really want is for Helix to be a console that is more powerful than the Series X I already own. I want the simplicity of console gaming, not the complexity that PC gaming often brings.

Does it allow access to other storefronts?:

I have said so many times that I think Xbox allowing store fronts like Steam on Helix would be a massive mistake. Once people realise that even brand new games on Steam often cost £10 less upon release than they do on Xbox, and once they see how games are cut more deeply in sales on Steam than they are on consoles, they will soon begin to make Steam their dominant library, and that will cost Microsoft billions in lost revenue, and given how Xbox is doing right now, that could easily sound the death knell for Xbox. Xbox needs to be making more money, not losing more still by enabling consumers to buy their games on Steam etc..

The only other thing that I would like an answer to right now is when Helix will launch. Rumour has it that the PS6 will release next year, and if the other rumour doing the rounds about Helix releasing in 2028 is true, then Helix will sink without a trace unless it is massively more powerful than the PS6, and considerably cheaper than it too. Helix needs to release at the same time as the PS6, or preferably a year before it, for it to stand a chance of success, particularly if Helix is basically a console because then that does mean that both the PS6 and Helix could be more or less on par in terms of power. As a PC, then it was always expected that Helix would be considerably more powerful than the PS6, but if both are consoles, then they may be much closer to one another in terms of power, which will probably favour PlayStation given the current userbase imbalance. It's going to be a difficult balancing act for Xbox when it comes to power and capabilities versus pricing, and how that stacks up to the PS6, but whatever happens, I really do not think that Helix can allow the PS6 a years head start.

Those are the three biggest questions that I have for Helix. I'm not overly concerned about the price because I want Helix to be my primary gaming platform even though I will be buying a PS6 too. With any luck, we will hear a lot more details within the next 6 months (unless Helix is releasing in 2028, in which case it'll be more like 18 months)...

There's also the battle over exclusive games. Xbox is expected to launch Helix with a strong lineup of exclusive titles, and the PS6 will likely do the same. But when you really think about it, even on that front PlayStation may already be at a disadvantage, since roughly 30-40% of the games available on Helix could be console exclusives to the platform, including not only Xbox first-party titles but also all the games that are released exclusively on PC, and there are a lot of those. Of course, that's talking about quantity and variety, which are already important advantages. The remaining question is game quality. And on that front, PlayStation needs to raise its game, because lately its first-party exclusives have not only been relatively few in number, but also haven't always lived up to expectations.

The next console war will also be decided by marketing and the public perception of the two brands. In that respect, PlayStation's reputation has taken quite a hit, while Xbox's image has become increasingly positive, particularly since Asha Sharma's arrival and the introduction of numerous player-friendly initiatives, such as Xbox Play Anywhere, lower Game Pass pricing, disc-to-digital support, a renewed focus on exclusive games, a stronger emphasis on consoles, the Rewards program, backward compatibility, and more.

These are all areas that distinguish Xbox from PlayStation, which, in comparison, doesn't seem to do much for its community other than ignore it.

#4049. NBA 2K27 Brings A Slice Of GTA 6's Vice City To Switch 2 This Month

A little-known curio called Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching this week; you may have heard of it. It's not releasing on Switch 2, of course, but that doesn't prevent any crossover content from making it our way. And so, welcome to the closest we'll get to GTA 6 on Switch 2, via NBA 2K27, of all places.

2K has just announced the forthcoming season of 2K27's online The City game mode, which'll feature an official crossover with Rockstar and GTA 6. Season 3 is all about Vice City, with Rockstar's already infamous take on the Miami streets making its way into online hooping sessions.

The season kicks off on 27th November, and includes a new Vice City-inspired Park and a bunch of new clothing and accessory items for your MyPlayer, like Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, and Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell Employee Outfits.

Here's a handful of screenshots of the event — none of which come from the Switch 2 version, obviously:

The open 'The City' mode is available in NBA 2K27 on Switch 2 (after the console missed out on the larger space in previous entries), though 2K still hasn't graced the hybrid with crossplay, so expect things to still be very quiet.

2K is marking the occasion with the digital release of the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition on 27th November. This one features Miami Heat's own Bam Adebayo on the cover, and comes bundled with a handful of extra perks (Season 3 Pro Pass, Vice City T-Shirt, 30 Skill Boosts, and 15 Gatorade Boosts).

So no, we won't be diving into GTA 6 on our Switch 2s any time soon, but hey, this is... something?

#4048. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4047. Grammy Awards Reveal This Year's Nominees for Best Video Game Soundtrack

The nominees for the 2027 Grammy Awards were recently announced, and of particular interest to gamers will be the shortlist for Best Score Soundtrack For Video Games and Other Interactive Media.

Five games, released between 31 August, 2025 and 28th August, 2026, are in contention, and two of them come from Sony's first-party efforts.

This could be a second Grammy for Gordy Haab, who jointly won for his work on Star Wars Jedi: Survivor in the 2024 awards.

PS Studios almost always has very strong music, so it's no surprise to see some representation here. Personally I can't speak to Marvel's Wolverine, but the score for Ghost of Yotei is great.

As for 007 First Light, to be honest I struggle to recall any of the music aside from the Bond theme and Lana Del Ray's title track.

It's an interesting group, anyway — I'm not sure I could really call it.

#4046. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4045. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4044. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score.

Did you pick up The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week? Let us know what you think of it so far in the comments below!

#4043. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4042. Rumour: Atlus May Be Gearing Up For A Huge Persona 6 Reveal

After what felt like an age waiting for the Persona franchise to make its Switch debut, Sega and Atlus are now all-in on the Switch 2. Persona 4 Revival is scheduled to launch on 20th May 2027, while Persona 6 has also been confirmed for the hybrid console.

Atlus is in full marketing mode for Persona 4 Revival, but our pals over at Push Square have reason to believe that the company may be gearing up to properly reveal Persona 6 in the coming weeks.

This comes from Reddit user ronakwya, who notes that Atlus recently updated the official website for Persona 6. Apparently, however, this was the kind of update that allows Atlus to perform significant changes to the website in preparation for a big public reveal.

Ronakwya has also pointed to the gameplay reveal of Persona 4 Revival as a potential hint. Its own website was also updated in a similar manner roughly one month prior to its big reveal at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026.

So, which big gaming event is taking place in just less than a month from now..? Yep, The Game Awards 2026.

This all seems incredibly convenient though, and to be honest we're a little sceptical. As pointed out by Push Square, it would make little sense for Atlus to pull attention away from Persona 4 Revival at this stage to host a full reveal for Persona 6.

In our opinion, we could definitely see a similar reveal during the Xbox Games Showcase in 2027 after the release of Revival in May (February for other platforms). We're happy to be wrong, as we're proper itching to see some gameplay from the next mainline entry, but we're not holding our breath.

#4041. Mini Review: Tanuki: Pon's Summer (PS5) - Easily One of 2026's Most Charming Adventures

Tanuki: Pon's Summer is a delight — and a finely crafted delight at that.

This is one of the most downright lovable indies I've played in a long time; it's a consistently charming concoction of semi-open world exploration, character stories, and minigames.

You play as the titular Pon, a lazy little tanuki who's tasked with repairing his god's shrine for the upcoming festival. But this is the kind of work that requires cash, and so our unlikely protagonist somehow snags a job at the local post office.

What follows is a day-to-day adventure across a rural Japanese island, where Pon must deliver packages to its inhabitants, and often lend a paw to their predicaments.

Oh, and Pon's also a BMX enthusiast, which means that he can take advantage of the landscape's many bike ramps and grinding rails to get around more (or less) efficiently.

There's a whole trick system that you can master, and while far from mandatory, pulling off sick moves as you go about your business nets you extra money at the end of your shift. Additional moolah lets you purchase more decorations for your shrine — which you're free to customise when you're not at work.

The relaxed process of cycling around the island, meeting quirky new characters, and taking part in an impressive variety of minigames — like fishing, bug catching, pint pouring, sushi stacking, and many others — is surprisingly moreish.

Indeed, developer Denkiworks has created something quite special in terms of structure. It feels like the game's always coming up with clever new ways to keep you entertained, which makes for a very nicely paced package.

That said, a few of the minigames can come across as slightly tedious. Picking up trash or sanding the bark off logs, for example, can't compare with landing a big fish, or partaking in a spot of sumo. Still, as alluded, it's hard to fault the variety that's on offer.

Lovingly put together and full of heart, Tanuki: Pon's Summer is a fantastic little slice of relaxation.
